notes:
Summary: Aether Content Foundry operates a 12M-article media archive (news + longform). Primary goal: fast, precise enterprise search for journalists and legal teams. Heavy emphasis on embeddings + reranking (RAG) to surface exact passages from long documents.

Scale & corpus: ~12M source docs, average doc length ~7k-12k tokens, many multi-GB PDFs and OCRed transcripts. Expected index growth ~20%/yr. Prototype target: index 1M doc sample (they estimate ~6-8M chunks w/ current chunking).

Performance targets: p50 search latency <= 120ms, p95 end-to-end <= 450ms (must meet p99 <= 900ms in evaluation). First-pass vector retrieval target 80-120ms; cross-encoder rerank should add <150ms when used (goal 100ms). Throughput target 150-250 QPS for newsroom peak. Cost sensitivity: want cost per query <= $0.015 on average; open to dedicated capacity to amortize cost.

Chunking strategy discussion (CRM notes):
- Prefer variable-length chunking with semantic boundary detection (paragraph/sentence-level) rather than fixed 1k-token windows to reduce noisy splits.
- Overlap strategy: 64-128 token overlap recommended by SE to capture context for reranker.
- Anchor metadata: article timestamp, section labels, OCR-confidence score to be kept with chunks for reranker features.
- POC plan: run 3 chunking passes on sample set (fixed 1k, variable-p, hybrid heuristics) and compare recall@10 / MRR and index size.

Embedding & index considerations:
- Candidate embed models: redwood-embed-v1 (dense), openembedding-large for comparison.
- Batch embedding pipeline: use continuous batching + prefix deduping; want streaming ingestion with checkpointed offsets.
- Index size estimate: sample suggests ~75M chunks for full corpus with current heuristics => storage + ANN CPU/GPU memory planning needed.

Reranker tuning (technical):
- They plan a two-stage setup: bi-encoder ANN first-pass (global) -> lightweight cross-encoder rerank for top-K (K=20). Trying to keep K small to control latency and cost.
- Metrics to optimize during POC: R@10, MRR, and answer-span F1 on labeled eval set (1.2k queries from internal newsroom). Also measure downstream latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Tuning levers discussed: K size, chunk overlap, reranker model size (distil cross-encoder vs full), prune by metadata score before rerank, and quantized inference on Dedicated GPUs.

Security & deployment notes:
- Must support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. Air-gapped option requested for archive with sensitive legal holds.
- Audit log retention 7 years for legal compliance; retention policy still under legal review.

Quotes/commitments:
- CTO Priya Rao: "We need sub-300ms p99 or this will fail editorial adoption."
- Head of Search Ops: "If Redwood can show cost per query < $0.02 at our scale we'll prioritize Dedicated procurement."

POC acceptance criteria (agreed):
- Demonstrate indexing of 1M sample with documented chunking configs and recall baselines.
- p95 end-to-end search <= 400ms on Dedicated trial for sample workload.
- Reranker increases nDCG@10 by >= 18% vs bi-encoder only on labeled queries.
- Cost projection with Dedicated that keeps expected cost/query <= $0.015 across projected QPS.

Action items (short):
- ACF to deliver curated 1M sample + 1.2k labeled queries (due 2026-03-12).
- SE (Avery) to run three chunking experiments and produce comparison report (due 2026-03-22).
- Infra to provision Dedicated trial (2x A100 equiv) for 4 weeks; security to complete KMS design review.
